raw_text:
Thanks — I’ll produce a 12-week general-fitness programme tailored for a 58-year-old male, six months post–myocardial infarction, cleared for moderate-intensity exercise only. I’ll keep aerobic work below ~70% of age-predicted max heart rate (~115 bpm), avoid Valsalva and maximal lifts, and prioritise safety, progressive overload within moderate intensity, and recovery. I’ll give phased progression, week-by-week sessions (3–4 gym sessions/week), exercises, sets/reps, tempo/notes, monitoring cues, and brief nutrition and recovery guidance.

Important safety reminders (deliver these to the client in writing and review before starting)
- Obtain written medical clearance for this specific programme from the client's cardiologist if not already provided.
- Monitor heart rate throughout sessions (chest strap or reliable wrist monitor). Keep heart rate below 115 bpm (70% age-predicted max). If the client uses beta blockers or other meds that affect HR, use perceived exertion (RPE) instead — target RPE 11–13 on the Borg 6–20 scale (light to somewhat hard).
- Avoid breath-holding and Valsalva on every lift; encourage slow, controlled breathing (exhale on effort).
- Stop exercise and seek medical attention if chest pain, undue shortness of breath, dizziness, palpitations, syncope, or unusual fatigue occur.
- Begin each session with a 8–10 minute warm-up (light aerobic + joint mobilisations). Finish with cool-down and stretching.

Program overview
- Length: 12 weeks, 3 sessions/week primary (full-body focus) with optional 4th light session (walking/recumbent bike/active recovery).
- Phases: Weeks 1–4 (Foundation: build tolerance, neuromuscular control), Weeks 5–8 (Strength & endurance: moderate progressive loading, increased volume), Weeks 9–12 (Consolidation & conditioning: maintain moderate intensity, add light metabolic work and functional tasks).
- Intensity: Moderate. Aerobic steady-state at <115 bpm or RPE 11–13. Resistance: light–moderate loads, 40–60% of estimated 1RM, controlled tempo (2–3s concentric, 2–3s eccentric), avoid max lifts; sets/reps designed for muscular endurance/hypertrophy without Valsalva.
- Progression: Increase reps, sets, or slightly increase load (~5% when client can complete top of rep range comfortably for two consecutive sessions) — but keep perceived intensity within safe limits.
- Sessions: each about 45–60 minutes including warm-up/cool-down.

Weekly structure (recommended)
- Monday: Session A — aerobic + full-body resistance
- Wednesday: Session B — aerobic + full-body resistance (different emphasis)
- Friday: Session C — aerobic + mobility/core + functional strength
- Optional Saturday or Sunday: light aerobic active recovery (20–40 min walking or recumbent cycling at easy pace <115 bpm)

Detailed weeks

Weeks 1–4: Foundation (goal = establish routine, build endurance and movement quality)
General guidance: Aim for 3 sessions/week. Keep HR within target during aerobic portions and monitor during resistance. Rest 90–120s between sets initially; breathing constant and controlled.

Week 1
Session A (Mon)
- Warm-up 8–10 min: treadmill walk 5–7 min easy (RPE 9–11), dynamic mobility (shoulder circles, hip hinges, ankle circles).
- Aerobic main: treadmill walking or recumbent bike 12 minutes continuous at easy–moderate pace (keep HR <115 bpm).
- Resistance circuit (2 rounds, rest 2 min between rounds):
  1) Seated machine chest press (or light dumbbell floor press) — 2 sets x 10–12 reps, tempo 2:2
  2) Seated row (machine or cable) — 2 x 10–12
  3) Goblet squat to a bench (bodyweight or light kettlebell) — 2 x 10–12 (no deep breath-hold)
  4) Standing overhead press with light dumbbells — 2 x 10 (avoid heavy loads; seated optional)
  5) Side plank (knees) or standing anti-rotation hold with band — 2 x 20–30s each side
- Cool-down 5–8 min: slow walk 3–5 min, gentle static stretches (hamstring, chest, calves) 20–30s each.

Session B (Wed)
- Warm-up 8–10 min: recumbent bike 6–8 min + mobility drills.
- Aerobic intervals (very gentle): 3 x (3 min slightly brisk, 2 min easy) — total 15 min — keep HR under threshold.
- Resistance (3 rounds, rest 90–120s between exercises if needed):
  1) Leg press (light) or split squat to box — 3 x 10
  2) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up — 3 x 10–12
  3) Dumbbell Romanian deadlift (light, hinge focus) — 3 x 10
  4) Standing biceps curls (light) — 3 x 12
  5) Seated abdominal curl or banded Pallof press (core anti-rotation) — 3 x 12–15
- Cool-down and stretching.

Session C (Fri)
- Warm-up 8–10 min: elliptical or brisk walk + shoulder/hip mobility.
- Aerobic: 18–20 minutes continuous at easy–moderate pace, HR <115 bpm.
- Functional strength & balance:
  1) Step-ups (low step) — 2 x 10 each leg
  2) Farmer carry (light dumbbells) 2 x 30–45s walk (focus posture, breathing)
  3) Single-leg stand with support 2 x 30s each leg
  4) Light machine or bodyweight hip extension / glute bridge — 2 x 12–15
- Cool-down and stretches.

Week 2–4
- Repeat similar structure. Progression options:
  - Week 2: increase aerobic duration by 5 minutes or add one more 3-min interval; add one extra set to resistance exercises (so 3 rounds where previously 2).
  - Week 3: increase resistance volume slightly (e.g., move sets to 3 for most exercises) while keeping loads moderate. Keep rest 60–90s between sets as tolerated.
  - Week 4: consolidate — keep similar volume to week 3 but introduce slight load increase if RPE remains low (5% increment) only if HR and breathing remain well controlled.
- Continue optional weekend brisk 20–30 min walk (easy pace).

Weeks 5–8: Strength & Endurance (goal = increase muscular capacity and aerobic time while maintaining safe intensity)
General: Increase to 3 sessions/week, consider adding optional 4th light session. Keep HR below threshold; training RPE 11–13. Resistance loads: moderate (40–60% 1RM), 3 sets typical, controlled tempo. Avoid Valsalva, encourage exhale on exertion.

Week 5
Session A
- Warm-up 8–10 min (treadmill or bike)
- Aerobic continuous: 25 minutes steady-state at easy–moderate pace (HR <115).
- Resistance (3 sets each):
  1) Machine chest press or dumbbell bench (light-moderate) — 3 x 8–10
  2) Seated cable row — 3 x 8–10
  3) Bulgarian split squat (bodyweight or light DB) — 3 x 8 each leg
  4) Dumbbell shoulder press (seated if needed) — 3 x 8–10
  5) Plank (knees or full) — 3 x 30–45s
- Cool-down.

Session B
- Warm-up 8–10 min
- Aerobic intervals: 4–5 repeats of (4 min steady at brisk but controlled pace, 2 min easy) — total 24–30 min — ensure HR returns to safe range during easy periods.
- Resistance (superset pairs to keep session efficient; rest 90–120s between supersets):
  1A) Leg press 3 x 10; 1B) Hamstring curl machine 3 x 12
  2A) Lat pulldown 3 x 10; 2B) Seated back-supported single-arm DB row 3 x 10 each arm
  3A) Cable triceps pushdown 3 x 12; 3B) Banded face pulls 3 x 12
- Cool-down.

Session C
- Warm-up 8–10
- Aerobic: 30 min steady state or recumbent bike 25–30 min
- Functional/core:
  1) Wall sits or light goblet squat 3 x 30–45s
  2) Farmer carry 3 x 45–60s
  3) Bird-dog progressions 3 x 10 each side
  4) Standing calf raises 3 x 12–15
- Cool-down and stretching.

Weeks 6–8
- Progression: Increase either time (aerobic sessions up to 30–35 min) or slightly increase resistance by small increments when client can complete top reps with good breathing and HR in range. Introduce light unilateral work and slightly more functional tasks. Keep RPE and HR guidelines strict.
- By week 8, target is comfortable 30–35 minute aerobic sessions at moderate pace and resistance work 3x8–12 across exercises.

Weeks 9–12: Consolidation & Conditioning (goal = improve functional fitness, endurance and confidence)
General: Keep intensity moderate; add light metabolic circuits if tolerated (shorter rests) while watching HR. Continue to avoid max efforts and Valsalva. Sessions remain 3x/week plus optional recovery.

Week 9
Session A
- Warm-up
- Aerobic pyramid: walk 5 min, brisk 5 min, easy 3 min, brisk 5 min (total 18) — increase total to 30 min across week.
- Resistance (3 sets):
  1) Dumbbell bench press or machine — 3 x 8–10
  2) One‑arm DB row — 3 x 10 each
  3) Reverse lunge to box — 3 x 8 each leg
  4) Overhead press with moderate DBs (focus breathing) — 3 x 8–10
  5) Standing Pallof press (anti-rotation) — 3 x 10–12 each side
- Cool-down.

Session B
- Warm-up
- Aerobic: interval set — 5 x (4 min moderate, 2 min easy) — ensure HR recovers toward baseline on easy intervals.
- Circuit (3 rounds, rests 90–120s between rounds):
  1) Step-ups 12 total
  2) TRX row or ring row 12
  3) KB deadlift or dumbbell Romanian deadlift 10–12
  4) Seated shoulder press machine 10–12
  5) Core: dead bug 12 each side
- Cool-down.

Session C
- Warm-up
- Aerobic: 30–35 min continuous steady state
- Mobility & balance emphasis:
  1) Single-leg RDL with light support 2 x 8–10 each
  2) Glute bridge progression 3 x 12–15
  3) Farmer carry + short stair/slope 3 x 45–60s
  4) Gentle stretching and breathing exercises (diaphragmatic breathing practice) 5–10 min
- Cool-down.

Weeks 10–12
- Week 10: similar to week 9 with small volume increases (e.g., add one circuit round or +5 minutes aerobic).
- Week 11: consolidate gains. Keep resistance at moderate load; focus on movement quality and breathing. Consider a slightly shorter rest between sets (60–90s) to gently increase conditioning but watch HR.
- Week 12: deload/assessment week — keep volume 10–20% lower. Use sessions to assess endurance (e.g., a comfortable 30–35 minute walk under threshold), strength (ability to perform 3 sets with moderate load), mobility improvements, and confidence. Provide home program for maintenance.

Sample exercise notes and safety cues
- Breathing: inhale on easier phase, exhale on exertion (e.g., exhale when pushing/pulling). Practice diaphragmatic breathing for respiratory efficiency.
- Avoid breath-holding. Cue client every set to breathe.
- Load selection: choose a weight that feels "moderate" and allows proper breathing and control. If HR rises toward 115 bpm during a resistance set, pause, rest, and reduce load or increase rest intervals.
- Tempo: 2–3s concentric, 2–3s eccentric. Focus on smooth controlled motion.
- Avoid heavy compound max lifts (no 1RMs, no heavy deadlifts or heavy single-leg loading beyond tolerated).
- Use machines and supported positions when necessary (e.g., seated press vs. standing to reduce strain).

Monitoring and progression rules
- Track HR and RPE during all sessions. Use RPE 11–13 as main guide if HR unreliable.
- If HR exceeds threshold for >2 minutes or RPE >13 persistently, reduce intensity and consult cardiology if unsure.
- Progress by increasing time (aerobic) first, then volume (sets/reps), then small load increases (5%). Do not increase more than one variable at once.
- If any adverse symptoms, stop and seek medical review.

Nutrition guidance (brief)
- Aim for a balanced diet emphasizing:
  - Adequate protein: ~1.0–1.2 g/kg bodyweight/day (adjust to client habit and renal status), spread across meals to support muscle maintenance.
  - Plenty of vegetables, whole grains, legumes, healthy fats (olive oil, nuts), and lean proteins (fish, poultry, legumes).
  - Limit sodium intake if advised by cardiologist; follow any specific cardiac dietary restrictions (e.g., fluid limits, potassium monitoring).
  - Hydration: sip regularly; avoid large boluses of water immediately before heavy exertion.
  - Moderate weight loss if indicated: aim for slow, steady deficit (0.5–1% bodyweight/week) supervised alongside medical advice.
- If on cardiac medications (statins, beta blockers, ACE inhibitors), be aware of potential interactions with exercise capacity and symptoms (monitor fatigue, muscle soreness, HR response).

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: target 7–8 hours/night.
- Stress management: include breathing exercises, light walking, and daily mobility to reduce sympathetic load.
- Active recovery day: light walking, gentle yoga, mobility; avoid strenuous activity on consecutive days if fatigued.
- Encourage regular medical follow-up and communicate exercise progress with the patient’s cardiology or rehab team as appropriate.

Sample 12-week weekly summary (concise)
- Weeks 1–2: 3x/week, 12–20 min aerobic + 2 rounds resistance, focus on breathing, RPE 10–12.
- Weeks 3–4: 3x/week, 20–25 min aerobic + increase to 3 sets for many exercises, introduce mild unilateral tasks, RPE 11–13.
- Weeks 5–8: 3x/week, 25–35 min aerobic sessions, intervals introduced, resistance 3 sets x 8–12, functional carries and balance work, progress loads modestly.
- Weeks 9–11: 3x/week, aerobic 30–35 min or interval sessions, circuits allowed if HR controlled, maintain moderate load, focus on conditioning and function.
- Week 12: deload and assessment — reduce volume ~10–20%, test steady-state aerobic for 30–35 min under threshold, review strength and mobility, plan ongoing maintenance.

If you want
- I can convert the above into printable weekly sheets for the client (session cards), with exact exercises per day for all 12 weeks.
- I can adapt the programme if he’s on beta blockers (switch to RPE-based targets), has hypertension, orthopedic limitations, or specific weight-loss/strength goals.
- I can suggest specific machines or names if you prefer a gym equipment list (e.g., treadmill, recumbent bike, leg press, cable row, chest press, lat pulldown, adjustable bench, dumbbells 2–30 kg, kettlebells, TRX).

Would you like the full 12-week session-by-session sheet laid out as printable cards, or any adaptations for medications/orthopedic issues?
